# Clouseau plugin API

> Clouseau is a desktop log viewer (Java 21, Swing). Plugins add log parsers, message formatters,
> syntax highlighters and live log sources. This page has everything needed to write one: the
> build file, the four extension points and their rules, and the command that checks a plugin
> without opening the app. It covers plugin API 0.3.0 (`com.droidenx.clouseau:clouseau-api` on
> Maven Central).

Source: https://github.com/benlazaro/clouseau. The API's Javadoc: https://javadoc.io/doc/com.droidenx.clouseau/clouseau-api.
A complete example plugin (a logfmt parser and a demo live source, with tests):
https://github.com/benlazaro/clouseau/tree/main/clouseau-example-plugin. Its folder builds on its
own when copied.

Before writing a parser, check that you need one: a format a regular expression can describe
needs no plugin. The user creates it in Clouseau's parser editor (Tools > Parser Editor...). Plugins are
for formats a regex can't express, and for formatters, highlighters and sources.

## Build

A Gradle project (Gradle 8, run on JDK 17 or 21). `settings.gradle.kts`:

```kotlin
rootProject.name = "acme-clouseau-plugin"
```

`build.gradle.kts`:

```kotlin
plugins { java }

val pluginId      = "acme-clouseau-plugin"   // must be <name>-clouseau-plugin
val pluginVersion = "1.0.0"
val clouseauApi   = "0.3.0"

repositories { mavenCentral() }
java { toolchain { languageVersion.set(JavaLanguageVersion.of(21)) } }

dependencies {
    // compileOnly: Clouseau provides both at runtime. Never bundle them (no fat/shadow JAR):
    // a JAR with its own copy of the API classes has extensions Clouseau doesn't recognize.
    compileOnly("com.droidenx.clouseau:clouseau-api:$clouseauApi")
    compileOnly("org.pf4j:pf4j:3.16.1")
    // Writes META-INF/extensions.idx from @Extension classes; without it no extension is found.
    annotationProcessor("org.pf4j:pf4j:3.16.1")

    testImplementation("com.droidenx.clouseau:clouseau-api:$clouseauApi")
    testImplementation("org.pf4j:pf4j:3.16.1")
    testImplementation("org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter:5.10.3")
    testRuntimeOnly("org.junit.platform:junit-platform-launcher")
}

tasks.test { useJUnitPlatform() }

tasks.jar {
    archiveBaseName.set(pluginId)            // the JAR must be named <Plugin-Id>-<Plugin-Version>.jar
    archiveVersion.set(pluginVersion)
    manifest {
        attributes(
            "Plugin-Id"          to pluginId,
            "Plugin-Version"     to pluginVersion,
            "Plugin-Requires"    to ">=$clouseauApi",
            "Plugin-Name"        to "Acme",               // optional, shown in the Plugin Manager
            "Plugin-Description" to "Reads Acme logs",    // optional
            "Plugin-Provider"    to "Your name",          // optional
            "Plugin-License"     to "MIT",                // optional
        )
    }
}
```

`gradle jar` builds `build/libs/acme-clouseau-plugin-1.0.0.jar`. To install it, copy it into the
`plugins` folder of Clouseau's data folder (Tools > Plugins... has a button that opens it). New
tabs use it right away; no restart.

Every extension class is `public`, has a public no-argument constructor, implements one of the
interfaces below, and is annotated `@org.pf4j.Extension`. One JAR may hold any number of them.

## Check it

```
java -jar clouseau-edge.jar --check-plugin build/libs/acme-clouseau-plugin-1.0.0.jar sample.log
```

`clouseau-edge.jar` is https://github.com/benlazaro/clouseau/releases/download/edge/clouseau-edge.jar
(Java 21). The check opens no window and runs while Clouseau is open. It loads the JAR as Clouseau
does and checks the manifest and the extension index, and whether the JAR bundles the API. Then it
runs each parser on the sample's lines: what it reads, entries without times or levels, whether it
throws or returns null, how timezones are handled, whether it's thread-safe, and which lines a
built-in parser takes first. It runs formatters and highlighters on the sample's messages, and
checks a source's settings. Each line of the report starts with OK, WARN, FAIL or NOTE, and the
report ends with `Result: N problems, M warnings`. The exit code is 0 when nothing failed and 1
when something did. Fix every FAIL and run it again. Give it a sample log of the format the plugin
is for, with a few lines of other formats, continuation lines (stack traces) and edge cases in it.

## LogEntry (what a parser returns)

An immutable class. Build it with `LogEntry.builder(rawLine)`, setting only what the format has:

```java
LogEntry.builder(rawLine)            // rawLine: the line as in the log, without its terminator
        .timestamp(instant)          // java.time.Instant; null if the line has none
        .level(LogEntry.LogLevel.WARN)  // TRACE DEBUG INFO WARN ERROR FATAL UNKNOWN; null = UNKNOWN
        .logger("com.acme.Orders")
        .thread("main")
        .message("order created")    // the text after the line's header; null = rawLine
        .field("order", "ORD-42")    // any other value; each field name becomes a table column
        .build();
```

`entry.toBuilder()` gives a builder with an entry's values. Never use the constructor.

## LogParser: a log format

```java
@Extension
public class AcmeParser implements LogParser {
    public String getName() { return "Acme"; }               // unique among all parsers
    public boolean canParse(String rawLine) { ... }          // is this line in my format?
    public LogEntry parse(String rawLine) { return parse(rawLine, ZoneId.systemDefault()); }
    public LogEntry parse(String rawLine, ZoneId writtenIn) { ... }   // Clouseau calls this one
    public List<String> customFields() { return List.of("order", "user"); }  // optional
}
```

- `canParse` runs on every line of every file during auto-detection: look at the line's start or
  a few characters, never parse it fully, and never throw.
- Auto-detection tries the built-in parsers and the user's own first, then plugin parsers, and
  takes the first whose `canParse` says yes and whose `parse` returns an entry. So a plugin can't
  take over lines a built-in format already reads; a user can still choose any parser for a tab.
- A line no parser reads becomes a continuation line of the entry before it (stack traces,
  wrapped text). So `canParse` must say no to continuation lines.
- Timezones: `writtenIn` is the timezone the log was written in (the user can change it). Read a
  timestamp with no offset as wall time in `writtenIn`. A timestamp with an offset or zone (`Z`,
  `+02:00`, `[Europe/Paris]`) keeps its own. `DateTimeFormatter.withZone(writtenIn)` does both:
  an offset in the text wins over it. Implement `parse(rawLine, writtenIn)`, and have the
  one-argument `parse` call it with `ZoneId.systemDefault()`. Only implement `parse(rawLine)`
  alone if the format's times never have an offset: the default `parse(rawLine, writtenIn)` then
  moves its result from the system's timezone to `writtenIn`, which shifts times that have one.
- Threads: one instance serves every tab, called from several background threads at once (never
  the Swing thread). Keep it stateless: no mutable fields, `DateTimeFormatter` (thread-safe), not
  `SimpleDateFormat`; compiled `Pattern`s are fine, shared `Matcher`s aren't.
- Failures: if `canParse` or `parse` throws, or `parse` returns null, the line shows as unparsed.
  Return null rather than a half-filled entry when a line turns out not to be yours.
- `customFields()` lists the field names in the order their table columns should have. Fields an
  entry has that aren't listed still get columns, added once rows with them are read.

## LogFormatter: rewrite a message for the detail panel

```java
@Extension
public class HexFormatter implements LogFormatter {
    public String getName() { return "Hex"; }           // the detail panel's toggle button
    public boolean canFormat(String input) { ... }      // quick look, not a parse
    public String format(String input) { ... }          // never null; return input if unsure
}
```

- It only changes what the detail panel shows for the selected entry (pretty-print, decode,
  unescape). The table, filters, find and copy keep the message as logged.
- Input: the entry's message, with any continuation lines appended after `\n`. Every formatter
  whose `canFormat` accepts the text so far runs in turn, each on the previous one's output: the
  built-in JSON and toString() formatters first, then plugin formatters.
- It runs on the Swing event thread: keep it fast (well under a few milliseconds for a typical
  message), no I/O, no state.
- If it throws or returns null, it's skipped for that message.
- Don't use the built-in names "JSON", "toString" or "Stack Trace". A formatter and a highlighter
  with the same name share one toggle button; give a formatter's highlighter its name.

## LogSyntaxHighlighter: color parts of a message

```java
@Extension
public class KeyValueHighlighter implements LogSyntaxHighlighter {
    private static final Pattern PAIR = Pattern.compile("(\\w+)(=)(\\S+)");

    public String getName() { return "Key=Value"; }
    public boolean canHighlight(String text) { return PAIR.matcher(text).find(); }
    public List<Span> highlight(String text) {
        List<Span> spans = new ArrayList<>();
        Matcher m = PAIR.matcher(text);
        while (m.find()) {
            spans.add(new Span(m.start(1), m.end(1), Role.KEY));
            spans.add(new Span(m.start(2), m.end(2), Role.OPERATOR));
            spans.add(new Span(m.start(3), m.end(3), Role.STRING));
        }
        return spans;
    }
}
```

- It gets the text after the formatters ran. `Span(start, end, role)` is a half-open character
  range `[start, end)` of that text; spans may come in any order; never return null (return
  `List.of()`).
- It names what text is, never a color: the theme colors each `Role`. Roles: `KEY` (the name in a
  name/value pair), `STRING`, `NUMBER`, `LITERAL` (true, false, null, enum constants), `KEYWORD`
  (a word that gives the structure: a segment name, a tag, a command), `OPERATOR` (a separator
  with meaning: `=`, `->`, HL7's `^ ~ &`), `PUNCTUATION` (brackets, braces, commas, delimiters),
  `MUTED` (text that matters less: raw bytes, padding, comments), `ACCENT` (something to notice
  among muted text), `ERROR` (an invalid value).
- Mark only what it recognizes. Every highlighter that accepts a message colors it, layered;
  where spans overlap the narrower wins.
- Runs on the Swing event thread: fast, no I/O, no state. If it throws, the message shows uncolored.

## LogSourceProvider and LogSource: live lines from somewhere

```java
@Extension
public class QueueSourceProvider implements LogSourceProvider {
    public String getName() { return "Acme queue"; }   // File menu: "Open Acme queue..."
    public List<SourceSetting> settings() {
        return List.of(
                SourceSetting.text("host", "Host"),
                SourceSetting.number("port", "Port").withDefault("5672"),
                SourceSetting.password("token", "Access token").optional(),
                SourceSetting.choice("from", "Start at", List.of("now", "beginning")).withDefault("now"));
    }
    // On the Swing thread: check the values and build the source; no I/O here.
    // Throw IllegalArgumentException with a message for the user if a value is wrong.
    public LogSource create(Map<String, String> values) { return new QueueSource(values.get("host"), ...); }
}

public class QueueSource implements ConnectingLogSource {
    public String getName() { return "acme: orders"; }    // the tab's status bar
    public void open(Consumer<String> lines, Runnable onConnected) throws Exception {
        connectAndSignIn();             // throw if it fails: Clouseau shows the message
        onConnected.run();              // at most once, from this thread: the tab's dot turns green
        while (!closed) lines.accept(nextLine());   // block; return when the stream ends or close() is called
    }
    public void close() { closed = true; /* and unblock open() */ }
}
```

- Clouseau draws the form from `settings()`, checks required fields and numbers, and remembers the
  values (passwords encrypted). Optional values left empty are absent from the map.
- `open` runs on a background thread and blocks, passing each raw line, without its terminator,
  in order. `close` comes from another thread, maybe more than once, maybe before `open` connected.
- A plain `LogSource` (one-argument `open(Consumer<String>)`) works too; its dot turns green at the
  first line.
- A source is used once: Reconnect calls `create` again with the same values. Keep connection
  state in the source, not the provider (one provider instance is shared).

## Publishing

Name the artifact `<name>-clouseau-plugin` under your own group (`io.example:acme-clouseau-plugin`);
`clouseau-<name>-plugin` is reserved for the Clouseau project's own. Publish it to Maven Central,
then add it to https://github.com/benlazaro/clouseau/blob/main/plugins.json with a pull request so
the Plugin Manager's Browse tab lists it. On a company Nexus, the name alone is enough.

## More

- User guide for plugin authors: https://benlazaro.github.io/clouseau/guide/developers.html
- Each API release's notes (what changed): https://github.com/benlazaro/clouseau/releases (tags `api-v...`)
